text.p: The chief financial officer of Reebok International Ltd said on Thursday that he supports Wall Street analysts' consensus earnings estimates of $2.59 per share for 1997.
"We are comfortable with what the Street is saying," the executive, Ken Watchmaker, said in an interview at an analyst meeting during the annual Super Show trade exhibition.
Reebok has been troubled for the past two years but another executive of the athletic footwear supplier told analysts that 1997 will mark the beginning of a turnaround.
"1997 will be the year we will finish laying the blocks for long-term sustainable growth," said Bob Meers, president of the Reebok brand.
The company plans to introduce three new shoes this year based on separate technologies.
